questions.q: Why must the markets be kept separate?
options: So consumers who buy cheaply can't resell to those who pay more
questions.why: Resale, or arbitrage, would bring the two prices together.

questions.q: A price-discriminating firm sets MR = MC in each separate market.
questions.why: This gives a higher price where demand is less elastic.

questions.q: Which is a likely benefit of price discrimination?
options: Some consumers who were priced out can now buy
questions.why: Lower prices for some groups can bring them into the market, though others pay more.

questions.q: Explain why a firm charges a higher price in a market where demand is price inelastic.

ideas.label: Consumers there aren't very sensitive to price
So a higher price raises revenue and profit

questions.model: Consumers in that market are not very sensitive to price, so quantity falls by less than the price rises. A higher price therefore raises revenue and profit.
questions.why: Inelastic demand: the price rise outweighs the lost sales.

tests.answer: Consumers have few substitutes so a higher price raises revenue and profit.
